title: Florida Electric Utility AI Infrastructure Opportunity
infrastructure_class: Electric utility generation, transmission, distribution, and data-center mechanical infrastructure
problem_statement: The profile proposes that AI data-center growth may increase Florida utility baseload, generation, transmission, distribution, and cooling requirements over an 18–36 month horizon; the magnitude, locations, sponsors, procurement paths, and specific projects are not yet evidenced.
analyst: S.P.A.T.I.A.L. Engine intake from Opportunity Profile.docx

evidence.claim: AI data centers are a material driver of Florida electric-utility infrastructure demand for this opportunity.
evidence.notes: The profile asserts the driver but provides no dated filing, plan, announcement, load forecast, or project record.

evidence.claim: Baseload growth, generation expansion, and water constraints create actionable infrastructure needs.
evidence.notes: No measured load, capacity, water, location, schedule, or consequence evidence is attached.

evidence.claim: Florida Power & Light, Duke Energy Florida, and JEA are reachable target utilities for the opportunity.
evidence.notes: The entities are named, but no sponsor, buyer, procurement authority, budget owner, or active requirement is identified.

evidence.claim: FPSC plans, Determination of Need proceedings, IRP updates, and hyperscaler announcements will expose relevant trigger events.
evidence.notes: These are plausible source and trigger categories, but no specific current trigger record is cited.

evidence.claim: Generation FEED, combined-cycle, nuclear, gas, 230/500 kV transmission, routing, substations, feeders, liquid cooling, direct-to-chip cooling, and HVAC are expected contract classes.
evidence.notes: The profile lists broad contract classes without tying them to a project, buyer, acquisition vehicle, technical requirement, or scope.

evidence.claim: The opportunity has an 18–36 month actionable time horizon.
evidence.notes: No dated event, procurement milestone, regulatory schedule, or construction critical path supports the horizon.

evidence.claim: Current authoritative evidence from FPSC filings, utility plans, regulatory dockets, earnings calls, and hyperscaler announcements supports the opportunity.
evidence.notes: The profile names source categories, but no specific evidence artifacts are included.

problem_evidence.rationale: The profile identifies plausible pressures, but it does not establish a measured infrastructure problem or observable consequence.

authority_clarity.rationale: Three target utilities are named, but the sponsor, buyer, budget owner, procurement authority, and approving authority are unknown.

technical_fit.rationale: Broad infrastructure and contract categories are listed, but no bounded project, site, load, system constraint, dependency, or solution pathway is defined.

funding_path.rationale: No budget, rate-case recovery path, procurement vehicle, solicitation, capital plan, customer payment mechanism, or eligible applicant is identified.

strategic_alignment.rationale: The evolving evidence-list concept fits infrastructure opportunity intelligence, but the profile does not define a bounded AnchorFiber or Sirius Logic Systems delivery role.

differentiated_advantage.rationale: Continuous evidence maintenance could differentiate the intelligence workflow, but no buyer-relevant advantage or comparison with incumbent tools is demonstrated.

delivery_readiness.rationale: No delivery team, utility relationship, licensed engineering partner, procurement path, data access, or phased work plan is identified.

risk_position.rationale: The profile exposes useful research categories, but decisive claims remain assumptions or unknowns and the scope spans several specialized infrastructure domains.

S.rationale: The market, sector, opportunity type, regulatory model, and initial target utilities are bounded at a lead-profile level.

P.rationale: Plausible pressure categories are named, but no measured condition, affected asset, or consequence is evidenced.

A1.rationale: Target organizations are named without a reachable sponsor, buyer, budget owner, procurement authority, or approver.

T.rationale: Potential work domains are listed, but no bounded technical requirement, project, site, dependency map, or delivery schedule is established.

I.rationale: No investment, funding, procurement, or implementation pathway is supplied.

A2.rationale: The evidence-intelligence concept is aligned, but the company's bounded role, advantage, partners, and commercial offer remain undefined.

known_limitations: The source document is a concise lead profile, not an evidence packet.
The document's High confidence label is not traceable to specific dated evidence.
No current utility filing, load forecast, regulatory docket, capital plan, hyperscaler announcement, solicitation, or project record is attached.
The profile combines generation, transmission, distribution, and mechanical scopes that may require separate opportunity records.
No bounded AnchorFiber, AnchorIntel, or Sirius Logic Systems commercial role is defined.
No engineering, regulatory, procurement, financial, or market conclusion is verified by this assessment.

lifecycle.next_action: Build a dated evidence packet for one target utility and one bounded project or trigger before authorizing outreach or proposal work.
lifecycle.resource_ceiling: Desk research only; no proposal, partner commitment, customer outreach, or engineering spend authorized
revalidation_triggers: A specific FPSC filing or regulatory docket is identified
A target utility publishes a quantified load or capital requirement
A hyperscaler announces a Florida site with utility or schedule detail
A solicitation, supplier event, or procurement vehicle is confirmed
A bounded Sirius Logic Systems role and delivery partner are defined
